section_name: Regression through the origin and additive correction of fixed predictions

candidates.title: Remember to Correct the Bias When Using Deep Learning for Regression!
candidates.reason: Closest direct match: estimates an additive output bias while retaining the remaining model parameters. Its residual-mean correction specializes to c=mean(y-2x)=3 on the supplied observations. This correspondence establishes no external-model limitation or future-data guarantee. Published in KI–Künstliche Intelligenz; DOI: 10.1007/s13218-023-00801-0.

candidates.title: Regression through the Origin
candidates.reason: Influential teaching paper explaining zero-intercept restrictions, their normal equations, and evaluation. Directly contextualizes the retained baseline 2x. Regression through the origin does not generally imply constant residuals; the residual of 3 follows specifically from the supplied y=2x+3. Published in Teaching Statistics; DOI: 10.1111/1467-9639.00136.

candidates.title: Fitting Regression Models with No Intercept Term
candidates.reason: Classic treatment of appropriate applications and pitfalls of no-intercept regression. Relevant to explaining the baseline's intercept restriction, while distinguishing estimation of regression slopes from the supplied calculation, which holds the slope at 2 and estimates only an additive correction. Published in Journal of Quality Technology; DOI: 10.1080/00224065.1977.11980770.

candidates.title: Leverage and Regression through the Origin
candidates.reason: Analyzes the relationship between intercept and no-intercept models using augmented-data leverage. Provides precise context for imposing a zero intercept without asserting that such models universally leave constant errors. Its model-comparison formulation differs from retaining the supplied prediction rule unchanged. Published in The American Statistician; DOI: 10.1080/00031305.1983.10482728.

candidates.title: Generalized Linear Models
candidates.reason: Foundational likelihood and score-equation treatment underlying residual balance when an intercept is estimated. Our specialization of its Normal identity-link formulation to the transformed responses y-2x gives intercept-only least squares and the residual mean. The five-point example is this specialization, not an example reported by the authors. Published in JRSS Series A; DOI: 10.2307/2344614.

candidates.title: Intercept corrections and structural change
candidates.reason: Influential analysis of additive forecast adjustments based on recent residuals or their averages while retaining model coefficients. Closely related to residual-mean correction, although its dynamic forecasting and structural-change setting extends beyond the supplied same-observation calculation. Published in Journal of Applied Econometrics, volume 11, pages 475–494.

candidates.title: Bias regularization in neural network models for general insurance pricing
candidates.reason: Develops post-training corrections that restore aggregate prediction balance, including adjustment of the output intercept. Relevant to estimating a constant after fitting the remaining prediction structure. Its canonical-link formulation requires attention to the scale of adjustment; a link-scale intercept shift need not be additive on the response scale. Published in European Actuarial Journal; DOI: 10.1007/s13385-019-00215-z.

candidates.title: The balance property in insurance pricing
candidates.reason: Recent focused treatment whose simple post-processing method shifts one intercept while retaining all slope coefficients and matching weighted observed and predicted totals. Its balance equation reduces algebraically to a residual-mean correction under an identity link and equal weights. Published in Scandinavian Actuarial Journal, first online September 2025; DOI: 10.1080/03461238.2025.2552909.

candidates.title: A Novel Approach to Forecasting After Large Forecast Errors
candidates.reason: Recent treatment explicitly using forecast-origin errors as intercept corrections with unchanged parameter estimates. Relevant conceptual context for adjusting a retained prediction rule, while distinguishing a one-time additive correction from subsequent detection and updating of trends. Published in Journal of Forecasting, first online October 2025; DOI: 10.1002/for.70062.

candidates.title: The Balance Property: The Constrained Case, with a View on Risk Sharing
candidates.reason: June 2026 theoretical preprint extending balance-correction analysis. Section 4.2 explicitly isolates an intercept shift with all remaining coefficients fixed, making it directly relevant current context. Its broader constrained-refitting analysis is separate from the supplied residual-mean calculation, and aggregate balance does not imply individually constant residuals. arXiv:2606.07276.
